title: Stop the retry scheduler from resending jobs that gave up

blocks.text: The retry scheduler keeps failed jobs in a list that it shares with the dispatcher. Before every dispatch round it should take out the jobs that have used up their attempts, so that the dispatcher stops resending them. Since the last release, some payout jobs are resent long after they gave up, and one round in a few hundred fails before sending anything.

Write `dropGivenUp(...)` in `src/main/java/practice/RetryQueue.java`. It takes every job for which `gaveUp(job)` is true out of the list it is given, the same list the dispatcher reads, and returns how many it took out. About three lines in total.
The tests call it with `ArrayList`s of jobs in various orders.

cases.says: with one job out of attempts, the method reports one job taken out
when every job has attempts left, nothing is taken out and the queue is unchanged
two jobs out of attempts that sit next to each other are both taken out
a job out of attempts at the front of the queue is taken out without the round failing
the list the dispatcher shares no longer holds the jobs that gave up

origin.section: removeIf Is the Safe Way to Remove While Iterating, and an Immutable List Refuses It Even When Nothing Matches

concepts: Collection.removeIf removes every matching element from the collection itself without skipping any, where removing inside an index loop or a for-each skips elements or throws ConcurrentModificationException.
